To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) people infer the popularity of an opinion based on its perceived fluency, (b) perceived fluency of an opinion is based on the fluency with which people think about the content of the opinion (the fluency of its content), and (c) perceived fluency is based on the ease with which people process the content of an opinion.
people can infer the popularity of a social norm from the ease with which they are able to generate examples of it.
The more frequently an opinion is expressed by a group member in a group discussion, the more frequently it is expressed by other group members in a subsequent group discussion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, What is it that leads people to believe that an opinion is more or less popular than they actually perceive it to be?
how people form impressions of the social world, and
the question of how people make inferences about the popularity of an opinion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the popularity of the opinion is inferred from the perceived popularity of the opinion.
the popular opinion on the subject is that the subject is not popular.
the popularity of a certain opinion or belief is inferred from the number of people who express that opinion or belief.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people infer the popularity of an opinion from its familiarity.
the mere exposure effect can be applied in the domain of attitudes and opinions.
people tend to overestimate the popularity of their own opinions, but underestimate the popularity of the opinions of their outgroup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people can infer the popularity of an opinion by simply thinking about the number of people who share it.
people can infer how popular an opinion is by simply thinking about the extent to which they are personally attracted to the opinion, and this inference can influence how they evaluate the opinion.
the popularity heuristic is an important factor in the way people form impressions about the prevalence of an opinion.
